desc: The ship foundered in the Atlantic Ocean off Trevose Head, Cornwall. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from Neath, Glamorgan to Teignmouth, Devon.

The ship ran aground at Llanelly, Glamorgan. She was on a voyage from Llanelly to Rouen, Seine-Inférieure, France. She was refloated and resumed her voyage, but put in to Pembrey, Carmarthenshire in a leaky condition.
The barque was driven ashore at Mersin, Ottoman Empire. She became a wreck on 11 February.
The tug was run into by a steamship and sank at Gravesend, Kent.
The ship was wrecked at Flamborough Head, Yorkshire. She was on a voyage from South Shields, County Durham to London.
The ship was driven ashore near Folkestone, Kent. Her crew were rescued.
The Thames barge collided with SS Cambridge (United Kingdom) in the River Thames at Belvedere, Kent and sank.
World War I: The cargo ship was sunk in the North Sea 30 nmi east of Aberdeen, United Kingdom by SMU U-25. Her sixteen crew survived.
The ship was driven ashore and severely damaged at Bergen. She was on a voyage from St. Ubes, Portugal to Bergen.

The full-rigged ship collided with the steamship Empire (United Kingdom) and sank in the English Channel off Hastings, Sussex, United Kingdom with the loss of two of her eighteen crew. Commerce was on a voyage from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States to Antwerp, Belgium.
The ship was driven ashore at Hayle, Cornwall.
The ship was driven ashore at Greenock, Renfrewshire. She was on a voyage from Bristol, Gloucestershire, to Greenock.
The sloop ran aground south east of Læsø, Denmark. She was on a voyage from Newcastle upon Tyne, Northumberland to Thisted, Denmark.
The ship was lost in the River Shannon with the loss of all hands. She was on a voyage from Liverpool, Lancashire to Terceira, Azores, Portugal.

The fishing dandy foundered between the Eddystone Rocks and Rame Head, Cornwall with the loss of three of the four people on board. The survivor was rescued by the fishing dandy Mary Jane (United Kingdom).
The yacht collided with the Mersey Flat Polly Williams (United Kingdom) and sank at Liverpool, Lancashire with the loss of one of her five crew.
The brig ran aground on the Shipwash Sand, in the North Sea off the coast of Suffolk and sank. Her crew were rescued by Jane Howard (United Kingdom).
note: Shipwash Sand placed at the centroid of Suffolk (the sand is not linked)

desc: World War II: The cargo ship was torpedoed and sunk in the North Sea 3 nmi north of Sheringham, Norfolk by German torpedo boat S-50 with the loss of nine of her crew.
The ship sank at the north end of Fair Isle, United Kingdom with the loss of all hands.
The four-masted auxiliary schooner was destroyed by fire off Southend, Essex. All nineteen crew survived.
note: Off Southend placed at the centroid of Essex

desc: The brig was driven ashore near Rhyl, Denbighshire. She was on a voyage from Saint John, New Brunswick, British North America to Liverpool.
The schooner was driven ashore at Lowestoft, Suffolk. Her six crew were rescued by the Coastguard using rocket apparatus. She was on a voyage from Middlesbrough, Yorkshire to Paignton, Devon.
The steamship was driven ashore on Inchkeith, Fife. She was on a voyage from Rotterdam, South Holland, Netherlands to Leith. She was refloated and completed her voyage.
The ship ran aground in the Clyde. She was on a voyage from Greenock, Renfrewshire to Quebec City, Canada.
The ship was driven ashore on Öland, Sweden. She was on a voyage from Riga, Russia to Bristol, Gloucestershire. Rose was refloated on 22 August and taken into Kalmar.
The schooner was driven ashore at Hollesley, Suffolk. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from Clacton-on-Sea, Essex to West Hartlepool, County Durham.
The ship was driven ashore and wrecked at Littlehampton, Sussex.
The ship capsized at Padstow, Cornwall.
The ship ran aground at Sunderland, County Durham. She was refloated and resumed her voyage, but put in to Whitby, Yorkshire the next day, where she sank.
The ship was lost near Mount's Bay. She was on a voyage from Dartmouth, Devon to Waterford, Ireland and Newfoundland, British America.

The schooner collided with HMS Bulldog in the English Channel off Eastbourne, Sussex and was damaged. She was taken in tow by HMS Bulldog but ran aground on the Boulder Bank and capsized. She was righted the next day and taken in to Newhaven, Sussex for repairs.

The brig ran aground on the Cross Sand, in the North Sea off the coast of Norfolk. She was on a voyage from Newcastle upon Tyne, Northumberland to Rouen, Seine-Inférieure, France. She was refloated with assistance from the tug Meteor and assisted in to Lowestoft, Suffolk.
note: Cross Sand placed at the centroid of Norfolk

desc: The brig was driven ashore north of Flamborough Head, Yorkshire. She was refloated and taken in tow for Scarborough, North Yorkshire by Ark (United Kingdom) but consequently foundered about 6 nmi off the coast. Her crew were rescued.
The steamship was driven ashore at Whitby, Yorkshire. She was refloated and towed in to Whitby but struck the quayside and developed a severe leak.
The ship was wrecked at Aldeburgh, Suffolk.
The ship capsized at Newport, Monmouthshire, United Kingdom.
The ship was wrecked at San Sebastián.
World War II: The cargo ship struck a mine and sank off Pola, Italy.
The ship was driven ashore and wrecked at New Romney, Kent. She was on a voyage from London to New Orleans, Louisiana.
The schooner was driven ashore and wrecked at Clifden, County Dublin. Her crew survived.
The ship ran aground and was damaged at Dover, Kent. she was on a voyage from Cephalonia, Greece to London.
The ship was driven ashore on Texel, North Holland, Netherlands. She was on a voyage from Drobak to Folkestone, Kent, United Kingdom. She was a total loss.
The schooner ran aground and sank at Aberystwyth, Cardiganshire. She was on a voyage from Gothenburg, Sweden to Aberystwyth.
The ship was driven ashore and wrecked at Whitby, Yorkshire.
The ship was abandoned on the Atlantic Ocean 400 nmi off Cape Clear Island, County Cork. Her crew were rescued by the schooner Gleaner (United Kingdom.
note: Abandoned 400 nmi off Cape Clear Island: the named place is only a reference point

desc: World War I: The cargo ship was torpedoed and sunk in the Tyrrhenian Sea off Stromboli, Italy by SMU UC-53.
The paddle steamer collided with RMS Ulster (United Kingdom) off Holyhead, Anglesey and was severely damaged. She was towed in to Holyhead by RMS Ulster.
The schooner was driven against the quayside and severely damaged at Stromness, Orkney Islands.
The brig was driven ashore in Gibraltar Bay near "San Felipe", Spain.

The schooner sprang a leak and sank about 5 nmi south west of the Longships Lighthouse, Cornwall. Her crew took to the ship's boat and were rescued by the St Ives Lifeboat, about 2 nmi off St Ives, Cornwall. Carvedras was on a voyage from Saundersfoot, Pembrokeshire to Truro, Cornwall.
The ship was driven ashore and wrecked at Tailor's Island, Isles of Scilly. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from London to Gibraltar and Cádiz, Spain.

The ship ran aground on the Warden Ledge, off the Isle of Wight, United Kingdom and was abandoned by her crew. She was on a voyage from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States to Berwick upon Tweed, Northumberland.
The brig was driven ashore on Inchkeith, Fife, United Kingdom. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from East Wemyss, Fife to Christiania.
The ship was driven ashore and severely damaged by fire near Le Touquet, Pas-de-Calais, France. She was on a voyage from the River Tyne to "Italy".
The barque was damaged by fire at Liverpool, Lancashire.

The ship was in collision with John and Sally (United Kingdom) and foundered in Mounts Bay. Her crew were rescued by John and Sally. St. Pierre was on a voyage from Noirmoutier, Vendée to Burry Port, Glamorgan, United Kingdom.

The schooner was driven ashore at St. Mawes, Cornwall. She was on a voyage from Plymouth Devon to São Miguel Island, Azores. She had been refloated by 3 January 1861 and taken in to Falmouth, Cornwall.
The ship was driven ashore on Texel, North Holland, Netherlands. She was bound for Genoa.
The ship foundered in the English Channel off Portland, Dorset with the loss of a crew member. Survivors were rescued by a French fishing vessel. She was on a voyage from Plymouth, Devon to London.
The ship foundered in The Downs. Her crew were rescued.
The schooner ran aground on Scroby Sands, Norfolk. She was on a voyage from Newcastle upon Tyne, Northumberland to Torquay, Devon.
The schooner was driven ashore and wrecked near Eyemouth, Berwickshire. All on board were rescued. She was on a voyage from Newcastle upon Tyne, Northumberland to Dundee, Forfarshire.
The ship was driven ashore and wrecked on Skagen before 15 December. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from Saint Thomas, Virgin Islands to Copenhagen.
World War I: The barque was sunk in the Atlantic Ocean 350 nmi west of the Skellig Islands by SMU U-157. Her crew survived.
World War II: The minesweeper struck a mine and sank off Esbjerg, Denmark with the loss of eight lives.
World War II: Soviet evacuation of Tallinn: The requisitioned 1423 GRT cargo ship (VT-563) was bombed and sunk southwest of Lavansaari by Junkers Ju 88 aircraft of Kampfgeschwader 77, Luftwaffe.
The ship foundered in the Irish Sea off the Saltee Islands, County Wexford in mid-April. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from Limerick to Belfast, County Antrim.
The steamship was driven ashore west of Dunkirk, Nord. She was on a voyage from Saint Petersburg, Russia to Dunkirk.
The ship was driven ashore at Sligo.
The steamship was wrecked on Anholt, Denmark. She was on a voyage from Kronstadt, Russia to London.
The steamship was driven ashore on Delos, Greece.

The steamship was driven ashore at Falsterbo, Sweden. She was on a voyage from Colberg to Hartlepool, County Durham, United Kingdom. She was refloated with assistance from the steamship Laura (Denmark) and taken in to Copenhagen.
The steamship ran aground at Havre de Grâce, Seine-Inférieure, France. She was on a voyage from New Orleans, Louisiana, United States to Hamburg.
The schooner was driven ashore and wrecked at Cockburnspath, Berwickshire. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from Sunderland, County Durham to Dundee, Forfarshire.
The sloop was driven ashore and wrecked west of North Berwick, Berwickshire. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from Eyemouth, Berwickshire to Glasgow.
The ship was driven ashore at Youghal, County Cork.
The brig was abandoned in the Atlantic Ocean. Her crew were rescued by the steamship SS Saxonia (German Empire). Lilian was on a voyage from Cardiff, Glamorgan to Imberwa, Brazil.
The sloop was wrecked near Slade, County Wexford, Ireland with the loss of all but two of her crew.
The brigantine ran aground at Ballyness, County Donegal and broke in two. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from Ballyness to London.
note: Ballyness placed at the centroid of County Donegal

desc: The ship was wrecked near Varberg, Sweden.
The ship was wrecked in the Isles of Scilly with the loss of sixteen of her seventeen crew. The survivor was rescued by a French vessel. She was on a voyage from Smyrna, Russia to London.
The schooner ran aground on the Gaa Sand, at the mouth of the River Tay. She was on a voyage form Sunderland, County Durham to Dunde, Forfarshire. She was refloated and taken in to Dundee.
The ship was driven ashore near Hjørring, Denmark. Her crew were rescued. She was on a voyage from Newcastle upon Tyne, Northumberland to Frederikshavn, Denmark.
The brig collided with the steamship Douglas (United Kingdom) off Gävle, Sweden. Fredrik Wilhelm was on a voyage from Sundsvall, Sweden to Aberdeen, United Kingdom. She was consequently condemned.
The ship was sunk by ice off Copenhagen, Denmark. She was on a voyage from Air to Memel, Prussia.

The brig was driven ashore in the Aran Islands, County Galway, United Kingdom. She was on a voyage from Odesa to Limerick, United Kingdom. She was refloated and towed in to Galway in a leaky condition.
The ship was wrecked near Llanelly, Glamorgan, Great Britain, with the loss of 89 of the 90 people on board. She was on a voyage from Newfoundland, British America, to Waterford.
note: Link [[Llanelly]] resolves to Llanelly, Monmouthshire (about 70 km inland of Llanelli); the text means Llanelli

desc: The dredger capsized at Le Havre, Seine-Inférieure.
The kuff was driven ashore and wrecked at Larvik, Norway. She was on a voyage from Helsinki, Grand Duchy of Finland to Schiedam, South Holland.
The ship was damaged by fire in the West India Docks, London.
The ship was driven ashore at Poole, Dorset. She was refloated the next day.
World War I: The cargo ship was sunk in the Atlantic Ocean 4 nmi south west of Hartland Point, Devon, United Kingdom by SMU U-60.
The steamship was driven ashore at Dimlington, Yorkshire. Her crew were rescued by a smack. She was on a voyage from Gothenburg, Sweden to London.
note: Dimlington placed at the centroid of the East Riding of Yorkshire

desc: The ship sprang a leak and was abandoned in the North Sea 70 nmi of Scarborough, Yorkshire. Her crew were rescued by Diadem (United Kingdom). Helena was on a voyage from Newcastle upon Tyne, Northumberland to Tønning, Duchy of Holstein.
note: Abandoned 70 nmi off Scarborough: the named place is only a reference point

desc: The barquentine was run into by the steamship Rona (United Kingdom) at Drummore, Wigtownshire and was beached. George was on a voyage from Maryport, Cumberland to Londonderry.
The schooner was wrecked on a reef north east of Islandmagee, County Antrim with the loss of all hands.
The ship was driven ashore on Læsø, Denmark. She was on a voyage from Halmstad Sweden to Leith. She was refloated and taken in to Fredrikshavn, Denmark.
The ship ran aground at Whitby, Yorkshire. She was later refloated.
The London-registered ship was driven ashore at Corton, Suffolk. Her crew were rescued. She was refloated in late December and taken in to Great Yarmouth for repairs.
The ship was beached at Memel, Prussia. She was on a voyage from Aberdeen to Memel. Granite was later refloated and taken in to Memel for repairs.
